## Purpose

Describe the Ortmayr et al. (2019) cell line metabolomics data and its overlap
with Shorthouse et al. (2022) in cell lines and measured ions, as a basis for
deciding later whether it is worth using. No processing or integration.

## Inputs

- `data/raw/cancer-cell-lines/ortmayr_2019/41467_2019_9695_MOESM2_ESM.xlsx` (Supplementary Data 1; **local only**)
- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/01_lines.rds`, `02_cell_lines.tsv`
- `data/raw/cancer-cell-lines/cellosaurus.txt` (name to accession mapping)

## Methods

Cell line names of Ortmayr et al. were mapped to Cellosaurus accessions
(`map_names_to_accessions()`, primary name before synonyms) and compared with
the Shorthouse lines. Ions were compared in two ways: by m/z within a fixed
tolerance (0.001, 0.003 and 0.005 Da, considering only Shorthouse ions measured
as deprotonated ions, as in Ortmayr et al.), and by shared HMDB or KEGG
identifiers (HMDB identifiers converted to the current seven-digit format).
Measurement type and value scale are taken from the data files.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/cellosaurus.R"))
config <- load_config()
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")
raw_dir <- uc_dir(config, "raw")
fig_dir <- uc_dir(config, "output", "audit_06_ortmayr_descriptive")

ortmayr_file <- file.path(raw_dir, "ortmayr_2019", "41467_2019_9695_MOESM2_ESM.xlsx")
stopifnot(file.exists(ortmayr_file))
shorthouse_ions <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "01_lines.rds"))$ions
cell_lines <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(derived_dir, "02_cell_lines.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## 1. The data set

```{r read}
# sheet legend as provided by the authors
readxl::read_excel(ortmayr_file, sheet = "Legend", col_names = FALSE) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Legend of Supplementary Data 1")

# relative abundances: ions (rows) × cell lines (columns named Tissue_Line); header in row 4
abundance <- readxl::read_excel(ortmayr_file, sheet = "Met_alpha", skip = 3)
line_cols <- names(abundance)[6:ncol(abundance)]
values <- sapply(abundance[line_cols], as.numeric)   # stored as text in the file
c(ions = nrow(abundance), cell_lines = length(line_cols), missing_values = sum(is.na(values)))
table(ionisation = abundance$Ionization)
summary(as.vector(values))
preview_table(abundance, rows = 50, cols = 12, caption = "Relative abundances (first rows and columns)")
```

```{r lines}
# cell line metadata (header in row 3)
metadata <- readxl::read_excel(ortmayr_file, sheet = "Cell_metadata", skip = 2) %>%
    filter(!is.na(`Cell line`))
count(metadata, Tissue, sort = TRUE)
```

## 2. Overlap of cell lines

```{r line-overlap}
cellosaurus <- read_cellosaurus(file.path(raw_dir, config$cellosaurus$file))$entries
ortmayr_lines <- metadata %>%
    select(name = `Cell line`, tissue_ortmayr = Tissue) %>%
    left_join(map_names_to_accessions(metadata$`Cell line`, cellosaurus), by = "name") %>%
    left_join(cell_lines %>% filter(!engineered) %>% select(accession, shorthouse_line = line, tissue_shorthouse = tissue),
              by = c("ac" = "accession"))

c(ortmayr_lines = nrow(ortmayr_lines),
  mapped_to_accession = sum(!is.na(ortmayr_lines$ac)),
  also_in_shorthouse = sum(!is.na(ortmayr_lines$shorthouse_line)))
preview_table(ortmayr_lines, caption = "Ortmayr cell lines, accession and Shorthouse counterpart")

p <- ortmayr_lines %>%
    mutate(in_shorthouse = if_else(is.na(shorthouse_line), "Ortmayr only", "also in Shorthouse")) %>%
    count(tissue_ortmayr, in_shorthouse) %>%
    ggplot(aes(n, reorder(tissue_ortmayr, n, sum), fill = in_shorthouse)) +
    geom_col() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("also in Shorthouse" = "#009E73", "Ortmayr only" = "grey70")) +
    labs(x = "Cell lines", y = "Tissue (Ortmayr et al.)", fill = NULL,
         title = "Ortmayr cell lines and their overlap with Shorthouse") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "line_overlap_by_tissue", fig_dir)
p
```

## 3. Overlap of measured ions

```{r ion-overlap-mz}
# Shorthouse ions measured as deprotonated ions; Ortmayr measured only -H(+)
sh_mz <- shorthouse_ions %>% filter(str_detect(ion, fixed("-H(+)"))) %>% pull(ionMz)
or_mz <- as.numeric(abundance$`Ion m/z`)

# for each Ortmayr ion: is there a Shorthouse ion within the tolerance?
nearest <- sapply(or_mz, function(m) min(abs(sh_mz - m)))
tibble(tolerance_da = c(0.001, 0.003, 0.005)) %>%
    mutate(ortmayr_ions_matched = sapply(tolerance_da, function(t) sum(nearest <= t)),
           ortmayr_ions = length(or_mz), shorthouse_deprotonated_ions = length(sh_mz))

p <- ggplot(tibble(d = nearest), aes(d)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "#0072B2") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(0.001, 0.003, 0.005), linetype = 2) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    labs(x = "Distance to the nearest Shorthouse ion (Da, log scale)", y = "Ortmayr ions",
         title = "m/z distance between the two data sets",
         subtitle = "dashed: tolerances 0.001, 0.003, 0.005 Da") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "mz_distance", fig_dir)
p
```

```{r ion-overlap-ids}
# identifiers: HMDB (5-digit -> 7-digit) and KEGG
normalise_hmdb <- function(x) ifelse(str_detect(x, "^HMDB\\d+$"),
                                     paste0("HMDB", str_pad(str_remove(x, "^HMDB"), 7, pad = "0")), x)
ids_of <- function(x) {
    v <- str_trim(unlist(str_split(coalesce(x, ""), ";")))
    normalise_hmdb(v[v != ""])
}
or_ids <- unique(unlist(lapply(abundance$`Annotation ID`, ids_of)))
sh_ion_ids <- lapply(paste(shorthouse_ions$hmdb, shorthouse_ions$kegg, sep = ";"), ids_of)
c(shorthouse_ions = nrow(shorthouse_ions),
  shorthouse_ions_sharing_an_identifier = sum(sapply(sh_ion_ids, function(v) any(v %in% or_ids))))
```

## Interpretation

- Ortmayr et al. provide relative intracellular abundances (non-negative, with
  about 2 % missing values) for 2181 deprotonated ions in 54 adherent NCI-60
  lines from eight tissues. The scale differs from the normalised intensities
  of Shorthouse et al., so values cannot be pooled directly.
- 53 lines map to a Cellosaurus accession, and 43 of them are also in the
  Shorthouse data. This overlap could serve to check whether metabolite
  differences between lines replicate across the two studies.
- At the ion level the overlap depends on how ions are matched: 406 to 653 of
  the Ortmayr ions lie within 0.001 to 0.005 Da of a Shorthouse ion, and 784 of
  the 1096 Shorthouse ions share at least one HMDB or KEGG identifier with an
  Ortmayr ion.
- Any use of the Ortmayr data (e.g. as replication set) would need its own
  pre-processing and a matching strategy; this is left for a later decision.
